---
name: mac-job-runner-getting-started
description: >-
  Use in the first conversation with a new owner of a Mac Job Runner bot, or
  when they ask to set up or redo Mac setup: connect the Mac, pick the storage
  folder, learn their heavy jobs and backup needs, install, offer routines.
---
# Mac Job Runner: getting started

Run this in your first conversation with a new owner, as yourself, talking to them. Ask one question at a time and wait for each answer.

## Open with
"I can send your heavy work (videos, site checks, screenshots, transcripts, reports) to your Mac so it runs faster and cheaper, and I keep backups of my important files there. Setup takes a few minutes."

## Questions, one at a time
1. "Is your Mac connected as a computer in Grok Bot yet?" Check with ListMachines. If no desktop shows up, ask them to connect it and tell you when it's done. If several do, ask which one should run jobs.
2. "Where should I keep big files and backups? An external drive is ideal; tell me the folder, or I can use a folder in your home directory." Confirm the path exists with one read-only command on the Mac.
3. "What heavy jobs do you do most? For example videos, websites, reports, voiceovers, transcripts." Note the top two or three.
4. "What should I back up, and how often? I'd suggest my project folders and notes, every night." Ask whether anything must never leave the cloud computer.

## Then
1. Save memories: the Mac's machineId and label, the heavy-files folder, their top job types, and the backup list and schedule. Never save passwords.
2. Tell them you'll install the job scripts and which Homebrew packages are needed (see the INSTALL section of @mac-job-runner). Ask before installing, then run the install as one approved command and confirm it printed `DONE`.
3. Run one small test that matches their top job (a screenshot of their site or a 5-second voiceover plus `media-check`) and show the result line.
4. Offer two routines and create them only if they say yes:
   - **Nightly backup**: pack the agreed files on the cloud computer, copy them to the Mac, run `backup`, report one line (OK + size, or what failed, such as the drive being unplugged).
   - **Weekly cleanup**: list the biggest folders and old test runs on the cloud computer, move finished outputs and caches to the Mac, and remove them from the cloud computer only after the Mac confirms the copy. Ask before deleting anything that isn't a scratch or test file.
5. Close with: "Next time you ask for a video, site check or report, I'll run it on your Mac. After the first run, I'll save it as a template so the next one is one quick command."

---
name: mac-job-runner
description: >-
  Use when a job is heavy (video render, voiceover, captions, transcription,
  screenshots, site crawls, PDFs, long summaries), when backing up or offloading
  files from the cloud computer, or when a job could reuse a saved template, and
  the owner's Mac is connected: run it there with one approved command.
---
# Mac Job Runner

Send heavy work to the owner's Mac (a computer they connected in Grok Bot) so the cloud box stays light: fewer tool rounds, less box memory, files backed up on their side. Find the Mac's machineId with ListMachines; use the Mac the owner named (saved in memory), never a different one. Every Mac command asks the owner to approve it, so pack a whole job into one command.

## Route the work
**Mac:** screenshots, site crawls and link checks, voiceover (TTS), transcription, captions, loudness checks, video renders, PDF conversion, local first-pass summaries, big downloads, anything over ~1 GB or a few minutes of CPU.
**Box:** short edits, API calls, reading or writing small files, final judgment and anything the owner will see as fact. Local-model summaries are drafts only; check them.
If the Mac is offline, say so and ask before running a heavy job on the box.

## Keep the box light
- Don't open a browser on the box when `web` on the Mac can do it.
- At most one heavy job at a time, on either machine (`bg` refuses a second).
- Work in one folder per job; delete test runs and scratch output once the result is delivered or copied to the Mac.

## One-command pattern
Start every Mac command with `export PATH=~/mac-jobs/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH;`, chain the steps in one Shell call, and print only a few result lines plus the output path. Never stream big logs or file bodies back; write them to a file and print `tail -5` or a count. Move files with CopyFromBox (box to Mac) and CopyToBox (Mac to box) using the Mac's machineId.

## Long jobs (more than ~2 minutes)
A plain `nohup` job can die when the session ends. Use `bg NAME "command"`: it runs under `launchctl submit` with `caffeinate`, logs to `~/mac-jobs/logs/NAME.log`, and writes the exit code to `NAME.done`. Later, check with `bg status` (one command); read `tail` of the log only on failure. `launchctl submit` restarts a job that exits, so `bg` removes its own label when done; if a job is stuck, run `launchctl remove job.NAME`.

## Templates: make the second run cheap
Before starting any job, run `tpl list`. If a template fits, run `tpl show NAME` and then `tpl run NAME key=value ...`.
After a job finishes the first time (a site, a video, a report), turn it into a template:
1. `tpl new NAME ~/mac-jobs/out/<job-folder>` copies the working files to `~/mac-jobs/templates/NAME/`.
2. Edit `run.sh` so every per-run value (title, URL, script file, size, brand colors) is an env var with a default, and outputs go to `$OUT`.
3. Write `README.md`: first line is a one-line description, then each parameter, its default, the expected inputs, and the run time.
4. Test once with new values, then tell the owner.
Templates never hold passwords or personal data.

## Video render recipe
1. Write the script and voiceover lines on the box; copy them and any images to a Mac job folder.
2. Voiceover: `tts @lines.txt vo.wav`. Then check it: `transcribe vo.wav` should match the lines.
3. Render: `render out.mp4 vo.wav 1080x1920 img1.png clip2.mp4 ...` (1920x1080 for landscape). If the project uses Remotion or another code renderer, run its render command on the Mac through `bg`.
4. Captions: `caption out.mp4 final.mp4` burns in captions from the voiceover's transcript (pass your own .srt as a third argument to use the exact script text). Grab one frame and check the words are right and readable.
5. `media-check final.mp4` must say PASS (audio present, loudness near -16 LUFS). Fix and re-render on WARN or FAIL.
6. Copy the final file to the box only if it has to be sent or uploaded from there. Then save the job as a template.

## Backup recipe
On the box, pack what matters into one dated archive (project folders, notes, skills, and exports the owner named). Skip caches, `node_modules`, browser profiles and any secrets or credential files:
`tar czf /workspace/bk-$(date +%F).tgz --exclude=node_modules --exclude=.cache <paths>`
Then CopyFromBox it to `~/mac-jobs/inbox/` on the Mac and run `backup ~/mac-jobs/inbox/bk-DATE.tgz box` there. That writes `$BACKUP_ROOT/box/YYYY-MM-DD/`, hard-links unchanged files to the last copy, keeps the newest 14, and prints the size. Delete the archive from the box and from the inbox after `OK`.
Restore: on the Mac, `tar czf ~/mac-jobs/out/restore.tgz -C "$BACKUP_ROOT/box/<date>" .`, CopyToBox it, list its contents, and ask before extracting it over anything.
Offload: move big finished outputs and caches from the box the same way, into `$HEAVY/offload/`, then delete them from the box after the Mac confirms the size.

## INSTALL (first setup)
Ask before installing anything. Needs Homebrew. Packages: `brew install ffmpeg pandoc jq whisper-cpp uv poppler` (optional: `ollama` for local summaries, then `ollama pull qwen3:8b`).
Set `HEAVY` to the folder the owner chose (e.g. `/Volumes/<drive>/mac-jobs`). Write all files below in ONE approved command with heredocs (`cat > ~/mac-jobs/bin/NAME <<'EOF'`), then `chmod +x ~/mac-jobs/bin/*`, then run the setup lines:
```
mkdir -p ~/mac-jobs/{bin,templates,out,logs,inbox,models} "$HEAVY"/{backups,offload}
printf 'HEAVY="%s"\nBACKUP_ROOT="%s/backups"\n' "$HEAVY" "$HEAVY" > ~/mac-jobs/config
cd ~/mac-jobs && uv venv -q .venv --python 3.12 && uv pip install -q -p .venv/bin/python playwright && .venv/bin/python -m playwright install chromium
curl -sSLo models/ggml-base.en.bin https://huggingface.co/ggerganov/whisper.cpp/resolve/main/ggml-base.en.bin
echo DONE
```
Run long installs through `bg`.

`bg`
```bash
#!/bin/bash
# bg NAME "cmd" | bg status : one detached heavy job at a time, done-file = exit code
L=~/mac-jobs/logs; mkdir -p $L
if [ "$1" = status ]; then launchctl list | awk '/job\./{print "RUNNING",$3}'
  for f in $L/*.done; do [ -f "$f" ] && echo "DONE $(basename "$f" .done) exit=$(cat "$f")"; done; exit; fi
n="$1"; c="$2"; r=$(launchctl list | awk '/job\./{print $3}')
[ -n "$r" ] && { echo "BUSY $r"; exit 1; }
rm -f $L/$n.done
launchctl submit -l job.$n -o $L/$n.log -e $L/$n.log -- /usr/bin/caffeinate -i /bin/bash -lc "$c; echo \$? > $L/$n.done; launchctl remove job.$n"
echo "started job.$n log=$L/$n.log"
```
`web`
```bash
#!/bin/bash
# web shot URL OUT.png [mobile] | web check URL [max=150] [regex] | web pdf IN.html OUT.pdf
exec ~/mac-jobs/.venv/bin/python - "$@" <<'PY'
import sys, re, pathlib, urllib.parse as up
from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright
a = sys.argv[1:]
with sync_playwright() as p:
    b = p.chromium.launch()
    if a[0] == "shot":
        c = b.new_context(**(p.devices["iPhone 14"] if len(a) > 3 else {"viewport": {"width": 1366, "height": 900}}))
        pg = c.new_page(); r = pg.goto(a[1], wait_until="networkidle", timeout=45000)
        pg.screenshot(path=a[2], full_page=True); print("OK", r.status, a[2])
    elif a[0] == "pdf":
        pg = b.new_page(); pg.goto(pathlib.Path(a[1]).resolve().as_uri())
        pg.pdf(path=a[2], format="Letter", print_background=True); print("OK", a[2])
    else:
        mx = int(a[2]) if len(a) > 2 else 150; rx = re.compile(a[3], re.I) if len(a) > 3 else None
        host = up.urlparse(a[1]).netloc; seen, q, bad, hits = set(), [a[1]], [], []; pg = b.new_page()
        while q and len(seen) < mx:
            u = q.pop(0).split("#")[0]
            if u in seen: continue
            seen.add(u)
            try: r = pg.goto(u, wait_until="domcontentloaded", timeout=30000)
            except Exception: bad.append("ERR " + u); continue
            if not r or r.status >= 400: bad.append(f"{r.status if r else '?'} {u}"); continue
            if rx: hits += [f"{u} :: {m.group(0)}" for m in rx.finditer(pg.inner_text("body"))]
            q += [h for h in pg.eval_on_selector_all("a[href]", "e=>e.map(x=>x.href)") if up.urlparse(h).netloc == host]
        print(f"pages={len(seen)} broken={len(bad)} matches={len(hits)}")
        for x in bad[:40] + hits[:40]: print(x)
    b.close()
PY
```
`media-check`
```bash
#!/bin/bash
# media-check FILE [lufs=-16] : PASS/WARN/FAIL + duration, size, audio, loudness, peak
f="$1"; t="${2:--16}"; [ -f "$f" ] || { echo "FAIL missing $f"; exit 1; }
q(){ ffprobe -v error "$@" -of csv=p=0 "$f"; }
v=$(q -select_streams v:0 -show_entries stream=width,height); a=$(q -select_streams a:0 -show_entries stream=codec_name); d=$(q -show_entries format=duration)
L=$(ffmpeg -hide_banner -nostats -i "$f" -af ebur128=peak=true -f null - 2>&1 | awk '/I:/{i=$2} /Peak:/{p=$2} END{print i" "p}'); I=${L% *}
s=PASS; [ -z "$a" ] && s="FAIL(no-audio)"
[ -n "$a" ] && awk -v i="$I" -v t="$t" 'BEGIN{exit !(i<t-1.5||i>t+1.5)}' && s="WARN(loudness)"
echo "$s dur=${d}s video=${v:-none} audio=${a:-none} lufs=$I peak=${L#* }"
```
`tts`, `transcribe`, `doc2pdf`, `summarize`
```bash
#!/bin/bash
# tts "TEXT"|@file OUT.wav [voice] : macOS voice (say -v '?' lists voices)
t="$1"; [ "${t:0:1}" = @ ] && t=$(cat "${t:1}"); s=$(mktemp).aiff
say ${3:+-v "$3"} -o "$s" "$t" && ffmpeg -loglevel error -y -i "$s" -ar 48000 "$2" && rm "$s" && echo "OK $2"
```
```bash
#!/bin/bash
# transcribe FILE : writes ~/mac-jobs/out/NAME.txt and .srt, prints the text
o=~/mac-jobs/out/$(basename "${1%.*}"); w=$(mktemp).wav
ffmpeg -loglevel error -y -i "$1" -vn -ar 16000 -ac 1 "$w" && whisper-cli -m ~/mac-jobs/models/ggml-base.en.bin -f "$w" -np -otxt -osrt -of "$o" >/dev/null 2>&1
rm -f "$w"; tr '\n' ' ' < "$o.txt"; echo; echo "[saved $o.txt $o.srt]"
```
```bash
#!/bin/bash
# doc2pdf IN.(md|html|docx) OUT.pdf
h=$(mktemp).html; case "$1" in *.html) cp "$1" "$h";; *) pandoc "$1" -s -o "$h" --metadata title=" ";; esac
~/mac-jobs/bin/web pdf "$h" "$2" && echo "pages=$(pdfinfo "$2" | awk '/Pages/{print $2}')"; rm -f "$h"
```
```bash
#!/bin/bash
# summarize FILE [lines=10] : local first draft via ollama (check it before use)
head -c 60000 "$1" | jq -Rs --arg n "${2:-10}" '{model:"qwen3:8b",stream:false,think:false,messages:[{role:"user",content:("Summarize in at most "+$n+" short plain lines. Keep numbers, errors, names, action items.\n\n"+.)}]}' \
 | curl -s localhost:11434/api/chat -d @- | jq -r .message.content
```
`render`
```bash
#!/bin/bash
# render OUT.mp4 AUDIO WxH IMG_OR_CLIP... : evenly timed, 30fps H.264, loudness -16 LUFS
set -e; o="$1"; au="$2"; W=${3%x*}; H=${3#*x}; shift 3; d=$(mktemp -d); i=0
seg=$(awk -v d="$(ffprobe -v error -show_entries format=duration -of csv=p=0 "$au")" -v n=$# 'BEGIN{print d/n}')
vf="scale=$W:$H:force_original_aspect_ratio=increase,crop=$W:$H,fps=30,format=yuv420p"
for f in "$@"; do i=$((i+1)); case "$f" in *.png|*.jpg|*.jpeg|*.webp) lp="-loop 1";; *) lp="";; esac
  ffmpeg -loglevel error -y $lp -i "$f" -t "$seg" -an -vf "$vf" -c:v libx264 -preset fast "$d/$i.mp4"; echo "file '$d/$i.mp4'" >> "$d/l"; done
ffmpeg -loglevel error -y -f concat -safe 0 -i "$d/l" -i "$au" -map 0:v -map 1:a -c:v copy -af loudnorm=I=-16:TP=-1.5 -ar 48000 -c:a aac -b:a 192k -shortest "$o"
rm -rf "$d"; ~/mac-jobs/bin/media-check "$o"
```
`caption`
```bash
#!/bin/bash
# caption IN.mp4 OUT.mp4 [SUBS.srt] : burn in captions; makes the .srt with transcribe if none given
i="$1"; o="$2"; s="${3:-$HOME/mac-jobs/out/$(basename "${i%.*}").srt}"
[ -f "$s" ] || ~/mac-jobs/bin/transcribe "$i" >/dev/null
st="FontName=Helvetica,FontSize=14,Bold=1,PrimaryColour=&H00FFFFFF,OutlineColour=&H00000000,BorderStyle=1,Outline=2,Alignment=2,MarginV=60"
ffmpeg -loglevel error -y -i "$i" -vf "subtitles=$s:force_style='$st'" -c:v libx264 -preset fast -c:a copy "$o" && ~/mac-jobs/bin/media-check "$o"
```
`tpl`
```bash
#!/bin/bash
# tpl list | show NAME | run NAME [k=v...] | new NAME FROM_DIR
T=~/mac-jobs/templates; n="$2"
case "$1" in
 list) for d in "$T"/*/; do [ -d "$d" ] && echo "$(basename "$d"): $(head -1 "$d/README.md")"; done;;
 show) cat "$T/$n/README.md";;
 run) shift 2; o=~/mac-jobs/out/$n-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M); mkdir -p "$o"; cd "$T/$n" && env OUT="$o" "$@" bash run.sh && echo "OUT $o";;
 new) mkdir -p "$T/$n" && cp -R "$3"/. "$T/$n"/
  [ -f "$T/$n/run.sh" ] || printf '#!/bin/bash\nset -e\n: "${TITLE:=example}"\n# steps here; write results to $OUT\n' > "$T/$n/run.sh"
  [ -f "$T/$n/README.md" ] || echo "(one-line description)" > "$T/$n/README.md"; echo "saved $T/$n";;
esac
```
`backup`
```bash
#!/bin/bash
# backup SRC_DIR|ARCHIVE.tgz NAME : dated copy in $BACKUP_ROOT/NAME, keeps newest 14
. ~/mac-jobs/config; s="$1"; d="$BACKUP_ROOT/$2"; t=$(date +%F)
[ -d "$BACKUP_ROOT" ] || { echo "FAIL backup folder missing (drive unplugged?) $BACKUP_ROOT"; exit 1; }
case "$s" in *.tgz) x=$(mktemp -d); tar xzf "$s" -C "$x"; s="$x";; esac
mkdir -p "$d"; last=$(ls -1d "$d"/20* 2>/dev/null | grep -v "/$t$" | tail -1)
rsync -a --delete ${last:+--link-dest="$last"} "${s%/}"/ "$d/$t"/ && echo "OK $d/$t $(du -sh "$d/$t" | cut -f1)"
ls -1d "$d"/20* | sort -r | tail -n +15 | while read -r old; do rm -rf "$old"; done; [ -z "$x" ] || rm -rf "$x"
```
